findings.title: A later tick can start a parallel run
findings.description: `Run.log` now recreates the run directory after state loss, but it does not restore or retain the active run's lock. If cleanup removes the state directory during review polling, the next tick can acquire a new lock and start another ticket; when the first run exits, `drop_lock` can remove that second run's lock while it is still active.

findings.title: Agent can run a script other than the runner's yt
findings.description: `agent_command` now allows `Bash(../bin/yt *)`, a path relative to the agent's working directory, not to the run directory. The agent can `cd` into a subfolder of the clone without a prompt, and that change persists. After that, `../bin/yt` points to `clone/bin/yt`, a path inside the clone that the agent can write. Any executable that ends up there runs on the host, outside the Docker sandbox, under the same allow rule.

findings.title: Existing ticks still use the cache folder
findings.description: `STATE_DEFAULT` changes the runner's fallback, but launchd supplies an explicit `YANTRA_STATE` from the plist generated at installation time. On a Mac with the previously installed agent, updating this checkout without reinstalling leaves ticks using `~/Library/Caches/yantra`, where the cleanup that prompted this change can still remove an active run's state.

findings.title: Docs and comments describe a macOS path the code does not use
findings.description: `runner.py` says 'The macOS path has a space, so each shell use of it needs quotes', and the very next comment says 'No space in the path'. The README also says 'The macOS path has a space'. Yet `STATE_DEFAULT` is `~/.local/state/yantra` on every OS, and the commit message promises `~/Library/Application Support/yantra` on macOS. A later reader cannot tell which default is intended. If someone 'fixes' the code to match the commit message, the path gets a space, the agent's full-path Bash rule then needs quotes, and the short `../bin/yt` rule this PR added becomes the only form that reliably matches.

findings.title: Crash tracebacks reach tick.log without token removal
findings.description: In `run_ticket`, the generic `except Exception` block now prints `traceback.format_exc()` straight to stderr. The handoff-failure block also prints `note` and a traceback there. Neither text goes through `TOKEN.sub`, the redaction that `Run.log` applies. For a tick, stderr is `tick.log`. Any exception whose message carries command output with a token, such as a `RuntimeError` built from `gh` stderr, is now written there in clear text.
